thread:
maria: noticing a weird spike in tail latency on the nightly inference smoke for head_dim=22, sm90, seqlen=1024. total p50 fine but p99 jumps ~3x. anyone seen this pattern?

jon: hmm, did the kernel picker change recently? which kernel was chosen when it spiked?

maria: looks like the picker flipped between flashv3 and sdpa-v2 during the run. repro log attached below. small repro command: 
```
./infer_bench --model redwood/7b --batch 8 --seqlen 1024 --heads 22 --device sm90 --warmup 10 --iters 50 --kernel-picker=auto
```

perf-bot: automated profile (1725000003): kernel_picker.probe detected oscillation: flashv3 -> sdpa_v2 -> flashv3 at iteration 14/50. KV cache warmup pattern: 3 microbatches showed cold KV misses.

maria: paste of microbench numbers from latest run: 
```
# iter,chosen,throughput_tok/s,latency_ms_p99
1,flashv3,98000,12
14,sdpa_v2,42000,35
15,flashv3,96000,13
30,sdpa_v2,43000,34
50,flashv3,97000,12
```

devon: interesting — head_dim 22 is not a multiple of 8 or 16, so flash kernels with vectorized lanes might be hitting unaligned tile code paths. Floors/ceilings in head-slice rounding can force a slow fallback. also sm90 has new tiling that prefers head remap for multiples of 2/4/8.

sam: +1. I hit something similar with head=14 on sm89 earlier. The kernel autotuner's latency heuristic uses throughput estimates that don't account for KV-cache-warmup penalties; if the picker probes during a warmup window it will pick an apparently slow kernel and stick.

olivia: can you dump the kernel picker trace (enable DEBUG=kernel_picker)? that shows the scoring and hysteresis decisions.

maria: enabled, trace below (snippet): 
```
[KER_PICK] iter=13 candidates=[flashv3,sdpa_v2,flashv2]
[KER_PICK] scores=[0.71,0.74,0.60] (sdpa_v2 chosen due to score+stability)
[KV] cache_hit_rate=0.42 warmup_count=3
[KER_PICK] hysteresis_window=8 last_switch=11
```

devon: score bump for sdpa_v2 likely came from lower p50 under short sample window. But when KV warmed up, flashv3 throughput recovers and is better for steady state. The picker needs workload-aware sampling (e.g., ignore samples with cache_hit_rate<0.6) or weight samples by steady-state tokens.

jon: alternative: add a bias toward kernels with better cold-start recovery when we detect KV misses (prefers kernels with faster KV fill). Is there a cheap proxy metric we can use? cache_hit_rate yes, and maybe "kv_miss_penalty_estimate" from recent iterations.

sam: quick experiment idea: change probe policy to require 2 consecutive probe wins before switching if warmup_count>1. reduces flip-flop. small patch: 
```
if (kv_warmup_count > 1) require_consecutive_wins = 2;
```

maria: ran that patch locally: 3 runs, no flip at iter14; steady throughput ~96k tok/s and p99 stable 12ms. patch diff in gist: https://internal/gists/ker-picker-warmup-hysteresis

olivia: nice. any downside? slower reaction to real workload shifts? might be acceptable as a canary. we should measure rollback time for real shifts.

devon: add arch-specific rules too: sm90 tends to prefer flashv3 once warmed because of vectorized INT8 paths; special-case head_dim % 4 != 0 to bias toward flash for seqlen>=512.

jon: let's land the hysteresis change behind a flag and run a canary on dedicated pool. name: KERNEL_PICKER_WARMUP_HYSTERESIS=1. Also add telemetry metric: picker_switch_reason and kv_warmup_count at switch.

maria: created PR #4821 with flag and telemetry. perf-bot will run perf job. PR diff small.

perf-bot: canary job queued (1725000036). expected runtime ~45m. alert if p99 > 20ms or picker flips > 3 times.

sam: one more thought — batching heuristics interact here too. when microbatching creates many small KV updates, the picker sample window should look at per-microbatch throughput not aggregated. otherwise sdpa gets credit from microbatch masking.

olivia: agree. add note to Optimize: recommend setting microbatch threshold for kernel probe > 2 microbatches.

jon: ok plan: (1) land flag-only change, (2) run canary, (3) if stable, enable by default + add head_dim special-case on sm90, (4) follow-up: refine probe scoring to include kv_hit_rate.

maria: thanks team — will follow up with canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: canary completed (1725000063): no flips observed, p99 median 12.3ms, throughput stable within 2%.

maria: great, setting rollout to 10% for next week and monitoring. :eyes:
